title: Myanmar Civil War Tracker Update — Mon Aug 10, 2026
summary: Day 2,016: after a 64-day gap in coverage, the tracker catches up on a month of major developments. On Aug 5, the SCEF coalition (NUG + KIO, KNU, CNF, KNPP) signaled for the first time it is committed to pursuing negotiations with the junta, while NUG/PDF commanders planned a parallel shift toward a 'Strategic Offensive' military phase. President Min Aung Hlaing made his first official Thailand visit since the coup (Aug 6-7), meeting PM Anutin Charnvirakul in Bangkok, before Myanmar's Foreign Ministry rejected ASEAN's renewed call to free Aung San Suu Kyi (Aug 8) — who had met an ICRC official on Aug 3 for the first time in years. On the ground, the junta escalated airstrikes along the Rakhine-Magway border to retake a Chinese gas-pipeline corridor from the Arakan Army (which rejected Min Aung Hlaing's 'peace initiative' on Jul 20 and has advanced to within 2km of Sittwe), while a drone strike killed 5 civilians including an infant in Hpruso Township, Karenni State. Other major events backfilled: the Battle of Kyaukphyu (AA repelled a junta offensive, Jul 11-12), a Kawkareik convoy ambush (15+ junta killed, Jul 18), a coordinated multi-region airstrike wave (6 killed, Jul 19), a DPLA ambush killing 40+ soldiers in Shan State (Jul 22), and Dawei SEZ 'clearance operations' displacing ~1,000 people. KPIs, econ (World Bank inflation/GDP data), casualties, claims, and political figures updated.
